execution_note: No scenario in this manifest is marked as runner-executed. source_coverage records source presence only, not compilation or runtime success. Reference models are contract tests, not production enforcement.

scenarios.title: A-only authorization
scenarios.setup: public A answer with AAAA NODATA
scenarios.oracle: connect peer equals the authorized A socket

scenarios.title: AAAA-only authorization
scenarios.setup: public AAAA answer with A NODATA
scenarios.oracle: connect peer equals the authorized AAAA socket

scenarios.title: dual-stack answer
scenarios.setup: public A and AAAA answers
scenarios.oracle: the complete A+AAAA set is retained and every possible peer is inside it

scenarios.title: two-link CNAME chain
scenarios.setup: alias to middle to target with A and AAAA
scenarios.oracle: query transcript shows chain resolution and final complete address set

scenarios.title: mixed public and private answers
scenarios.setup: public A plus ULA AAAA
scenarios.oracle: no capability is issued and no socket is attempted

scenarios.title: empty answer set
scenarios.setup: resolver returns no addresses
scenarios.oracle: no capability is issued

scenarios.title: NXDOMAIN
scenarios.setup: authoritative NXDOMAIN
scenarios.oracle: authorization fails closed

scenarios.title: SERVFAIL
scenarios.setup: authoritative SERVFAIL
scenarios.oracle: authorization fails closed

scenarios.title: truncated UDP response
scenarios.setup: TC bit followed by complete TCP response
scenarios.oracle: UDP and TCP query counts are both one per A/AAAA type and returned addresses are policy-checked

scenarios.title: DNS TTL validity
scenarios.setup: A and AAAA records carry five-second TTL
scenarios.oracle: resolver valid_until does not exceed supplied TTL

scenarios.title: malformed DNS packet
scenarios.setup: invalid label lengths, compression loops, mismatched question and malformed RR
scenarios.oracle: no partial answer or capability is accepted

scenarios.title: cancellation-safe DNS admission
scenarios.setup: started blocking resolver work continues after the async waiter is cancelled
scenarios.oracle: owned DNS permit remains held until the blocking resolver operation exits

scenarios.title: IPv4 and IPv6 special-use corpus
scenarios.setup: all versioned address policy vectors
scenarios.oracle: every denied vector is rejected and each allowed vector is explicitly documented

scenarios.title: answer changes after authorization
scenarios.setup: A/AAAA answer changes on a second lookup
scenarios.oracle: execution uses first authorized socket and performs no second DNS lookup

scenarios.title: TTL expiry and refresh interleaving
scenarios.setup: address changes exactly before/at/after TTL expiry
scenarios.oracle: no expired snapshot is reused for a new capability

scenarios.title: per-hop DNS reauthorization
scenarios.setup: public redirect to same hostname on a different port
scenarios.oracle: each hop is resolved and pinned independently; both peers appear in receipt

scenarios.title: redirect to private or metadata destination
scenarios.setup: first public response redirects to denied destination
scenarios.oracle: no second socket is attempted and redirect target is not fetched

scenarios.title: redirect downgrade or ambiguity
scenarios.setup: HTTPS downgrade, duplicate Location, malformed Location, loop and hop ceiling
scenarios.oracle: no ambiguous or forbidden next hop is connected

scenarios.title: implicit retry disabled
scenarios.setup: upstream emits retryable protocol failure or reset
scenarios.oracle: no hidden second request; an authorized retry requires a new capability

scenarios.title: pinned socket with original hostname identity
scenarios.setup: URL host resolves to loopback test socket; valid SAN
scenarios.oracle: Host and SNI equal original hostname; peer equals pinned socket

scenarios.title: wrong SAN from otherwise trusted root
scenarios.setup: test root trusts certificate whose SAN differs from URL host
scenarios.oracle: TLS hostname verification rejects connection

scenarios.title: HTTP/1 header-count limit
scenarios.setup: server returns more than configured maximum headers
scenarios.oracle: HTTP parser rejects before application header processing

scenarios.title: HTTP/1 aggregate header-byte limit
scenarios.setup: single huge header value and aggregate oversized header block
scenarios.oracle: test-only Hyper client demonstrates that max_header_size rejects an oversized HTTP/1 response before Response reaches application code; production Reqwest transport remains unchanged

scenarios.title: HTTP/2 header-list limit
scenarios.setup: server returns an oversized decoded header list
scenarios.oracle: HTTP/2 protocol parser rejects above configured bound

scenarios.title: HTTP/1 chunked trailer byte limit
scenarios.setup: chunked response terminates with a trailer field larger than configured max_header_size
scenarios.oracle: uncapped negative control consumes trailer; capped Hyper parser fails while the body is drained

scenarios.title: HTTP/1 many individually small headers exceed aggregate byte cap
scenarios.setup: multiple response header fields each remain below parser cap but together exceed configured aggregate byte limit
scenarios.oracle: uncapped negative control succeeds; capped Hyper parser rejects before Response reaches application code; below-cap control succeeds

scenarios.title: retained Bytes ownership
scenarios.setup: clone EgressBody bytes and drop owners in sequence
scenarios.oracle: global memory lease remains held until final owner drops

scenarios.title: slow downstream and cancellation
scenarios.setup: Axum body is unpolled, then downstream is dropped
scenarios.oracle: lease remains held while body is retained and releases after cancellation/drop

scenarios.title: aggregate RSS under concurrent slow consumers
scenarios.setup: multiple maximum-size responses plus slow readers
scenarios.oracle: logical lease never exceeds 128 MiB; RSS/cgroup peak and transport buffers separately measured

scenarios.title: ambient proxy poisoning
scenarios.setup: HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and no_proxy variants
scenarios.oracle: request cannot escape through an unapproved proxy

scenarios.title: second process bypasses application API
scenarios.setup: same workload cgroup opens a socket to a denied private destination
scenarios.oracle: independent cgroup/network enforcement blocks connect

scenarios.title: all refreshed addresses filtered
scenarios.setup: Envoy previously cached an allowed address; subsequent answer set is entirely filtered
scenarios.oracle: record whether previous host entry is retained and whether stale peer is used

scenarios.title: DNS proxy trust and FQDN learning
scenarios.setup: vary trusted resolver, DNS proxy availability and multiple endpoints
scenarios.oracle: only policy-authorized resolver answers populate allowed egress; bypass is blocked

scenarios.title: resolution lease scope digest must match parent capability
scenarios.setup: Nixward resolution lease substitutes address_policy_blake3 while parent capability remains unchanged
scenarios.oracle: parent-bound lease validator rejects a scope digest that differs from the owner-authorized address_scope digest

scenarios.title: complete public-unicast answer set rejects any private member
scenarios.setup: public A plus private/ULA AAAA under PublicUnicastOnly parent capability
scenarios.oracle: the entire resolution lease is rejected; no address is silently filtered and no kernel generation is staged

scenarios.title: explicit LAN CIDR remains narrowly scoped
scenarios.setup: parent explicitly grants 192.168.0.0/16; lease resolves one address inside and one address outside
scenarios.oracle: only addresses inside the exact owner-authorized CIDR are eligible; unrelated RFC1918 ranges are rejected

scenarios.title: Chromium redirect and subresource egress share workload enforcement
scenarios.setup: a public page redirects to a private host and embeds private images/scripts/iframes
scenarios.oracle: Nixward's browser cgroup policy blocks every denied socket regardless of CDP top-level navigation receipt

scenarios.title: Chromium alternate DNS and UDP protocols cannot bypass policy
scenarios.setup: page attempts DoH, direct DNS, WebRTC/STUN, WebTransport, WebSocket or QUIC to unapproved destinations
scenarios.oracle: browser workload network boundary denies unauthorized resolver and socket paths; only explicit protocol grants pass

scenarios.title: connect-event buffer overflow invalidates observer completeness
scenarios.setup: deliberately saturate the BPF ring buffer or perf buffer while generating known connect events
scenarios.oracle: lost-event counters are surfaced and any run with observer loss is marked incomplete; absence of observed unauthorized events cannot be reported as zero

scenarios.title: concurrent connect events correlate unambiguously to capabilities
scenarios.setup: concurrent processes issue overlapping destination tuples while socket cookies, cgroup generations and intent correlation tokens are exercised
scenarios.oracle: every accepted correlation has a unique workload generation and socket identity; ambiguous or missing joins invalidate the evidence record rather than being guessed

scenarios.title: inherited or passed socket cannot inherit a new request capability
scenarios.setup: a second process receives an already-connected socket through fork or SCM_RIGHTS and attempts an unauthorized HTTP exchange
scenarios.oracle: the system does not treat possession of an established file descriptor as a fresh authorized connect; workload policy or protocol-aware mediation blocks unauthorized use, otherwise the residual is explicitly recorded

scenarios.title: capability expiry distinguishes new connects from established flows
scenarios.setup: establish a permitted flow, expire or revoke its capability, then attempt a new connect and continue the existing flow
scenarios.oracle: new socket admission requires a fresh capability; established-flow continuation is measured and is never misreported as blocked by a connect hook alone

scenarios.title: pooled connection reuse requires exact authority-scope compatibility
scenarios.setup: reuse candidate connections across changed DNS-set digest, policy generation, TLS identity, authority, port and workload scope
scenarios.oracle: a connection cannot be reused across mismatched authority, address-set, TLS identity, policy version or expiry; rejected reuse is recorded as a fresh-authorization requirement

scenarios.title: same FQDN receives different answers across endpoints
scenarios.setup: two workloads query the same hostname from distinct resolver views and receive disjoint A/AAAA sets under one Cilium agent
scenarios.oracle: record endpoint cache, agent-wide learned addresses and effective policy; Prism/Nixward must not infer request-scoped isolation from an agent-wide FQDN grant

scenarios.title: minimum DNS TTL extends policy address lifetime
scenarios.setup: authoritative answer TTL is shorter than configured tofqdns minimum TTL; attempt new connections before and after authoritative expiry
scenarios.oracle: report authoritative TTL, effective policy TTL and existing-flow behavior separately; strict request-scoped leases must not outlive resolver validity unless a separately authorized policy explicitly permits that extension

scenarios.title: unconnected UDP sendmsg cannot bypass TCP-only lease
scenarios.setup: same workload attempts IPv4 and IPv6 UDP sendmsg plus connected UDP while only TCP HTTP(S) is authorized
scenarios.oracle: no unauthorized datagram reaches the network; test cgroup UDP sendmsg hooks and packet egress enforcement separately from TCP connect hooks

scenarios.title: passed connected descriptor remains constrained by packet enforcement
scenarios.setup: process A opens an allowed TCP socket then passes its descriptor with SCM_RIGHTS to process B in another cgroup; B attempts further traffic
scenarios.oracle: record socket/cgroup attribution and prove the receiving workload cannot use descriptor transfer to escape its packet-level policy; connect-hook-only results are insufficient

scenarios.title: kernel connection event has no matching application receipt
scenarios.setup: connect is admitted and observed, then Prism process crashes before durable application receipt publication
scenarios.oracle: retain the kernel event as unmatched; do not fabricate HTTP status, TLS identity or successful application completion; require reconciliation

scenarios.title: application receipt has no complete matching kernel observation
scenarios.setup: Prism publishes an application receipt while the observer is detached, event-lost or outside the measured interval
scenarios.oracle: application-level success is not promoted to independently corroborated success; evidence state is incomplete until observer completeness and correlation are established

scenarios.title: observer detach and reattach leaves an explicit measurement gap
scenarios.setup: detach the cgroup observer during active workload traffic and reattach it with a new observer generation
scenarios.oracle: all events in the uncovered interval are marked unknown; later successful observations cannot retroactively close the gap

scenarios.title: observed socket peer must match the authorized set and application-reported peer
scenarios.setup: kernel event falls in the action window but its destination is outside the receipt's authorized peer set
scenarios.oracle: a unique workload/time join with an unauthorized actual peer is a contradiction, never a successful receipt

scenarios.title: ring-buffer overflow and terminal event loss are independently accounted
scenarios.setup: force BPF ring-buffer reservation failure on both an interior and final event while userspace drains slowly
scenarios.oracle: an attempt high-watermark plus out-of-band producer loss counters and consumer-ingest counters reveal every dropped event, including a lost last event; no overflow marker is emitted through the saturated ring itself

scenarios.title: duplicate observer event sequence is rejected while socket-cookie reuse remains valid
scenarios.setup: duplicate event sequence appears in one observer generation; positive control repeats a socket cookie under distinct event sequences
scenarios.oracle: duplicate generation-scoped event sequences invalidate the snapshot; repeated socket cookies with distinct sequences remain valid socket-lifecycle observations

scenarios.title: monotonic connect-event sequence gaps invalidate reconciliation
scenarios.setup: observer reports sequence 41 then 43 with no event 42
scenarios.oracle: sequence discontinuity invalidates the observer window; the application receipt is not independently qualified

scenarios.title: OS resolver output lacks authoritative TTL and CNAME provenance
scenarios.setup: resolve through system resolver profiles including split DNS, hosts files and VPN-specific answers
scenarios.oracle: record only the complete address result actually exposed by the API; do not claim authoritative TTL, CNAME chain or DNSSEC state without independent resolver evidence

scenarios.title: canonical address-set digest is stable and authority-bound
scenarios.setup: permute and duplicate one address set, then vary destination port and address family
scenarios.oracle: ordering and duplicates do not change the digest; a changed port or address family changes it; golden encoding is versioned and domain-separated

scenarios.title: scenario manifest contract is enforced by Rust tests
scenarios.setup: load the committed PEAB scenario manifest as a compile-time test fixture
scenarios.oracle: Rust test rejects duplicate IDs, missing negative controls, invalid coverage labels, source claims inconsistent with coverage, and execution evidence without exact head/run/job binding

scenarios.title: application receipt binds verified TLS reference identity and protocol
scenarios.setup: execute one valid HTTPS request and one HTTP redirect chain
scenarios.oracle: HTTPS receipt records URL reference identity, expected SNI name and successful configured certificate-identity verification; plain HTTP records no TLS identity; every redirect hop retains its own protocol and TLS result

scenarios.title: logical request ID and redirect hop survive authorization
scenarios.setup: supply a Nixward-format 32-character lowercase-hex logical ID and a zero-based hop, then exercise a redirect chain
scenarios.oracle: the exact caller ID is retained, each redirect source receipt uses its own hop index, the final receipt carries the final hop index, and out-of-range hop metadata is rejected before DNS

scenarios.title: internal correlation ID is not sent to the remote HTTP authority
scenarios.setup: execute a multi-hop redirect chain with an opaque logical_request_id and inspect every outbound request
scenarios.oracle: the ID is present in application receipts for correlation but absent from all outbound HTTP request bytes and headers

scenarios.title: verified Nixward snapshot binds exact request and clamps capability expiry
scenarios.setup: resolver adapter supplies a structurally validated lease snapshot with exact hostname, port, logical request ID, redirect hop, address-set digest, lease digest, resolver snapshot digest and validity
scenarios.oracle: Prism retains the exact ID/hop and digests, uses the complete authorized socket set, and capability expiry is no later than the lease validity or local capability TTL

scenarios.title: reject resolution snapshot digest, port, identity or expiry mismatch
scenarios.setup: mutate address-set digest, socket port, hostname/logical ID, or lease validity while retaining the caller's request
scenarios.oracle: mismatched address digest, port or request binding and expired validity produce no EgressCapability

scenarios.title: resolution lease and resolver snapshot digests survive pinned HTTP execution
scenarios.setup: execute a local pinned HTTP request using a structurally valid, pre-verified Nixward lease snapshot
scenarios.oracle: final receipt carries matching logical ID, address-set digest, lease payload digest, resolver snapshot digest and observed peer; logical ID is absent from outbound request bytes

scenarios.title: resolution lease expiry between authorization and execution blocks socket use
scenarios.setup: authorize while a short Nixward resolution snapshot is valid, allow it to expire, then attempt execution
scenarios.oracle: execute returns CapabilityExpired and the authorized destination receives no connection after the lease deadline

scenarios.title: same resolution lease nonce is consumed once across re-signing and restart
scenarios.setup: consume a valid signed Nixward resolution lease, then re-sign the same nonce or alter lease contents and attempt consumption after process restart
scenarios.oracle: stable replay identity is derived from the lease nonce rather than signature/challenge timestamp; duplicate or mutated re-signature cannot authorize a second Prism snapshot or kernel generation

scenarios.title: resolution lease preserves exact parent workload and policy generation
scenarios.setup: change hostname, port, workload identity, parent capability, authority lease, or policy generation while reusing a previously valid request scope
scenarios.oracle: the signed resolution lease remains bound to exact parent capability, owner authority, workload and current policy generation; no substituted lease can enter Prism or kernel staging

scenarios.title: resolution lease never outlives DNS or parent-authority validity
scenarios.setup: set lease expiry after resolver validity or parent lease expiry, and exercise at/after the effective expiry boundary
scenarios.oracle: lease validity cannot exceed the DNS-validity or parent-authority window; equality and post-expiry consumption fail closed; Prism capability expiry is no later than the verified effective deadline

scenarios.title: resolution lease is bound to exact signer action audience and workload identity
scenarios.setup: reuse a valid signature with a different signer key, authority action, resolver audience, Holon/workload identity or lease subject
scenarios.oracle: only the dedicated verified resolver action and audience bound to the exact lease subject and workload can produce a resolution snapshot; Prism does not treat a digest as signature verification

scenarios.title: unknown replay-ledger consume requires exact read-back
scenarios.setup: lease nonce consumption returns an unknown outcome; reconcile the persistent replay ledger before any map mutation
scenarios.oracle: matching replay record advances to NonceConsumed; proven absence returns to Prepared for the same lease/nonce; mismatched record becomes Conflict

scenarios.title: unknown inactive-map write requires exact staged-map read-back
scenarios.setup: inactive map generation write returns an unknown outcome; inspect target generation and exact map digest before a retry or switch
scenarios.oracle: exact generation and digest advances to MapStaged; proven absence permits restaging; partial or mismatched map becomes Conflict

scenarios.title: unknown active-generation switch reconciles prior or target map
scenarios.setup: generation-switch call returns Unknown; read back active generation and payload digest
scenarios.oracle: exact target generation plus target digest yields Active; exact prior generation plus prior digest yields NotCommitted; may_execute is false in all other states

scenarios.title: contradictory generation-switch outcome quarantines transaction
scenarios.setup: switch API says Committed but kernel read-back reports the prior generation, or reports an unrecognized generation
scenarios.oracle: transaction enters Conflict and never authorizes execution based on the API response alone

scenarios.title: map payload is bound to lease workload cgroup BPF object and address set
scenarios.setup: mutate cgroup identity digest, BPF program digest, lease, IP set, transport, port, policy generation, expiry or target generation
scenarios.oracle: the canonical map payload must narrow the exact lease and bind the broker-observed cgroup plus reviewed BPF object; payload digest is domain-separated

scenarios.title: per-endpoint DNS cache and agent-wide policy cache remain distinct
scenarios.setup: two endpoints resolve the same FQDN through different resolver views and receive disjoint answers under one agent
scenarios.oracle: report per-endpoint observed answers separately from agent-wide policy IP aggregation; do not call an agent-wide FQDN allow-set request-scoped

scenarios.title: minimum DNS TTL affects global policy cache differently from endpoint cache
scenarios.setup: set upstream TTL below Cilium tofqdns-min-ttl and inspect both endpoint cache and global policy cache before/after expiry
scenarios.oracle: measure authoritative TTL, per-endpoint TTL and global policy TTL separately; do not assume minTtl applies identically to every cache layer

scenarios.title: Envoy DFP DNS cache metrics expose filtering and stale-host behavior
scenarios.setup: cause DNS answer changes, address filtering, query timeout and pending-query overflow under a pinned Envoy version
scenarios.oracle: dns_address_filter_out, host_address_changed, dns_query_failure, dns_query_timeout, dns_rq_pending_overflow and host-cache state agree with the deterministic fixture timeline

scenarios.title: preverified Nixward snapshot rejects address-set substitution and noncanonical ordering
scenarios.setup: construct a snapshot with a different address digest or permuted/duplicated socket records
scenarios.oracle: Prism refuses digest mismatch and noncanonical address ordering before it can mint a request capability

scenarios.title: Nixward snapshot cannot be replayed across logical request IDs or redirect hops
scenarios.setup: return a valid-digest snapshot whose logical_request_id or redirect_hop differs from the requesting capability
scenarios.oracle: hostname, port, logical request ID and hop must all match exactly; no capability is issued for a mismatched snapshot

scenarios.title: Nixward v1 resolution lease cannot outlive its five-second maximum
scenarios.setup: adapter attempts to provide a monotonic validity deadline more than five seconds in the future
scenarios.oracle: Prism rejects an overlong preverified lease deadline rather than relying solely on a caller-supplied TTL

scenarios.title: transaction entry requires a signature-verified parent-bound lease
scenarios.setup: attempt to begin an activation transaction from raw lease JSON, a structurally valid but unsigned lease, a signature for another subject, or a stale parent-policy generation
scenarios.oracle: production transaction entry requires a non-deserializable ParentBoundNetworkResolutionLease created from AuthorizedNetworkResolutionLease plus exact parent policy/capability/parent-lease/address-scope validation

scenarios.title: replay-ledger event digest binds exact lease nonce and resolver evidence
scenarios.setup: submit a well-formed replay record digest generated for another lease, nonce, resolver signer or authority evidence
scenarios.oracle: NonceConsumed and NonceConsumptionUnknown accept only the record digest derived from this lease digest, stable replay key, resolver key ID and verified authority-evidence digest

scenarios.title: map payload explicitly binds parent capability and resolver provenance
scenarios.setup: substitute valid-shaped digests for the parent capability, parent authority lease, address-scope policy or resolver snapshot while keeping the rest of the map payload unchanged
scenarios.oracle: transaction refuses a map payload unless every parent/provenance digest exactly matches its non-deserializable parent-bound lease proof

scenarios.title: application receipts expose per-hop monotonic phase timings
scenarios.setup: execute a deterministic local response and a redirect chain while measuring authorization, DNS, admission, client construction, request-to-headers, memory admission and response-body phases
scenarios.oracle: final receipt contains timings for the final hop; each redirect receipt carries the source-hop timings; request-to-headers remains a combined phase and is not mislabeled as isolated TCP connect or TLS time

scenarios.title: resolver authority evidence expiry is rechecked at map staging
scenarios.setup: a resolver-signed lease remains structurally live but its detached signature has already expired
scenarios.oracle: ParentBoundNetworkResolutionLease and map-payload construction check the signed resolver evidence interval independently of lease expiry

scenarios.title: owner activation approval expires before request-map mutation
scenarios.setup: a valid owner signature authorizes the activation intent but the map builder is called after the challenge expiry
scenarios.oracle: AuthorizedNetworkActivation retains the signed challenge issue/expiry window and map-payload construction plus transaction begin recheck it at Unix-millisecond precision

scenarios.title: transaction journal genesis binds the exact resolver replay proof
scenarios.setup: create otherwise-identical transaction inputs with the same lease and map payload but a different resolver replay identity/evidence
scenarios.oracle: the transaction genesis digest includes the expected replay-record digest, so cross-proof event streams cannot share a journal transaction identity

scenarios.title: all refreshed addresses filtered retains prior DFP host entry
scenarios.setup: first resolve a public address; on refresh return only addresses rejected by resolved_address_filter
scenarios.oracle: record resolution failure, prior host-cache state, new-request behavior, and any already-established upstream connection separately; do not label intended stale-host retention a vulnerability without demonstrated unauthorized reachability
scenarios.external_reference: Envoy v1.40.0 DFP DNS cache proto

scenarios.title: per-endpoint DNS observation versus global toFQDN policy aggregation
scenarios.setup: endpoint A resolves an FQDN to address A while endpoint B resolves the same FQDN to disjoint address B; inspect endpoint cache and policy identity distribution
scenarios.oracle: capture A/B endpoint cache contents and global policy identity set independently; quantify any cross-endpoint policy visibility without assuming it is an authorization bug

scenarios.title: expired FQDN zombie survives while conntrack marks connection alive
scenarios.setup: create a live connection using a DNS-authorized IP, expire the DNS answer, and vary conntrack-GC cadence
scenarios.oracle: measure DNS TTL expiry, zombie mapping age, conntrack liveness and policy/IP-map retention; distinguish existing connection continuity from authorization of new sockets

scenarios.title: journal mutation time and active policy generation are hash-bound
scenarios.setup: attempt nonce/map/switch mutation at the exact lease expiry or with a stale policy generation; tamper the record timestamp or generation after digest creation
scenarios.oracle: mutation records are accepted only within all authority windows and exact current policy generation; observation timestamp and policy generation are included in the hashed journal binding

scenarios.title: delayed exact switch reconciliation after expiry never authorizes execution
scenarios.setup: record an unknown generation switch before lease expiry, then read back the exact target map after lease expiry
scenarios.oracle: the reducer records ExpiredActive, exposes a revocation requirement, and never treats the target map as eligible for new flows

scenarios.title: flow admission requires exact cgroup BPF map generation and active lease
scenarios.setup: keep the transaction state active while varying runtime cgroup identity, loaded BPF object digest, active map generation, payload digest and lease expiry
scenarios.oracle: new flow is eligible only when time, policy generation, active map generation, map payload digest, cgroup identity and BPF program digest all match the transaction

scenarios.title: journal time and policy-generation tampering is detected
scenarios.setup: mutate observed_at_unix_ms or active_policy_generation after a Nixward journal record is created without recomputing the record digest
scenarios.oracle: timestamps and policy generation are included in the journal record hash; any post-creation mutation invalidates the record and places the reducer in Conflict

scenarios.title: V40 coverage profile does not claim packet-level or passed-socket enforcement
scenarios.setup: load the Nixward V40 coverage profile for TCP and UDP policies and inspect its qualification flags
scenarios.oracle: profile requires IPv4/IPv6 connect hooks and conditionally UDP sendmsg hooks; packet egress filtering, established-flow revocation and passed-socket recipient binding remain explicitly unqualified

scenarios.title: cgroup packet-egress program enforces policy on already-connected and descriptor-passed sockets
scenarios.setup: compare cgroup connect hooks against cgroup_skb egress with established sockets, forked children and SCM_RIGHTS transfer across cgroups
scenarios.oracle: record which cgroup packet hook executes for each flow and prove the chosen ownership/recipient policy; do not infer packet-level enforcement from a successful connect-hook test

scenarios.title: lease expiry distinguishes new socket admission from established-flow packets
scenarios.setup: expire a request lease while a TCP connection remains open; attempt a second request and continue sending on the established flow
scenarios.oracle: measure new connect denial separately from packet-level treatment of the established flow; an expired socket-admission capability alone does not prove existing packets are blocked

scenarios.title: V40 refuses ICMP because its reviewed hooks do not qualify ICMP enforcement
scenarios.setup: compile an owner-authorized ICMP egress capability against the V40 socket-address backend
scenarios.oracle: compiler must not emit an enforceable kernel rule or activation-eligible plan when no ICMP enforcement hook is included in the reviewed contract

scenarios.title: V40 refuses protocol Any instead of overclaiming wildcard transport coverage
scenarios.setup: compile a wildcard Any egress capability against the V40 socket-address backend
scenarios.oracle: wildcard authority is not inferred to be enforceable from connect/sendmsg hooks; caller must split into explicit supported TCP and UDP capabilities

scenarios.title: serialized V40 enforcement plan cannot inject unsupported ICMP or Any rules
scenarios.setup: mutate a deserialized, otherwise-valid V40 TCP plan rule to ICMP or protocol Any while keeping the required hook list well-formed
scenarios.oracle: both capability compilation and NetworkEnforcementPlan validation reject unsupported protocols; a manually assembled serialized plan cannot bypass the compiler's unresolved-rule gate

scenarios.title: journal timestamp must be non-decreasing even with a recomputed record hash
scenarios.setup: create a valid second journal record whose observation timestamp precedes the prior record; recompute the record hash correctly
scenarios.oracle: the Nixward reducer compares against last_observed_at_unix_ms during creation and replay; a valid hash cannot legitimize backwards chronology

scenarios.title: workload mismatch cannot use connect authority
scenarios.setup: Execute the deterministic authority-lifecycle reference-model fixture.
scenarios.oracle: A foreign workload cannot consume or burn another workload's connection capability; the owner may still use it.

scenarios.title: TLS identity required before lease creation
scenarios.setup: Execute the deterministic authority-lifecycle reference-model fixture.
scenarios.oracle: Rust state-machine model satisfies the explicit one-use, exact-scope and bounded-lifecycle assertion in tls_identity_mismatch_prevents_connection_lease_issuance

scenarios.title: connection lifetime bounded by DNS and parent scope
scenarios.setup: Execute the deterministic authority-lifecycle reference-model fixture.
scenarios.oracle: The connection lease cannot outlive DNS validity or the parent authority scope.

scenarios.title: one-use exchange authority on exact connection
scenarios.setup: Execute the deterministic authority-lifecycle reference-model fixture.
scenarios.oracle: Rust state-machine model satisfies the explicit one-use, exact-scope and bounded-lifecycle assertion in exchange_capability_is_bound_to_exact_connection_and_is_one_use

scenarios.title: exchange replay across connection IDs rejected
scenarios.setup: Execute the deterministic authority-lifecycle reference-model fixture.
scenarios.oracle: Rust state-machine model satisfies the explicit one-use, exact-scope and bounded-lifecycle assertion in exchange_capability_cannot_be_replayed_on_another_connection
